transit_basis: Deep-draft vessels, normal capacity (EIA). ~13,000-14,000/yr in a normal year; fell to 9,944 deep-draft transits in the FY2024 drought.
share_world_trade: ~2.5-5% of world seaborne trade by volume (UNCTAD/McKinsey; IMF).
primary_cargo: Containers, petroleum products & hydrocarbon-gas liquids, dry bulk (grain, coal), vehicles.
dominant_vessels: Container ships, LPG (VLGC) & LNG carriers, chemical/product tankers, bulk carriers, car carriers.
top_users: United States (~66-75% of cargo), China, Japan.
local_economic_note: Canal revenue ~US$5.0bn (FY2024); ~4% of Panama GDP and ~20% of central-government income (ACP; AS/COA).
reroute_note: Alternatives: Suez (+~7-10 days) or Cape of Good Hope; US Gulf->China is ~+20 days via the Cape.

transit_basis: All vessels, 2023 record year (Suez Canal Authority). Traffic roughly halved to 13,213 transits in 2024 during the Red Sea crisis.
share_world_trade: ~12-15% of world trade and ~30% of global container traffic (UNCTAD).
primary_cargo: Containerized manufactures (Asia-Europe), crude & refined products, LNG, dry bulk, vehicles.
dominant_vessels: Container ships, tankers (~32-37% of transits), dry bulk carriers, LNG and car carriers.
top_users: Asia-Europe carriers (Maersk, MSC, CMA CGM); operated by Egypt.
local_economic_note: Toll revenue US$10.3bn (2023) fell to ~US$4bn in 2024 (-60%); a top source of Egypt's foreign currency (SCA; Ahram Online).
reroute_note: Alternative: Cape of Good Hope, +~3,000-3,500 nm / +10-14 days, ~+US$1M fuel per voyage.

transit_basis: All vessels, 2024, Malacca and Singapore Straits COMBINED (inforMARE). Not directly comparable to single-strait counts.
share_world_trade: ~one-quarter of world seaborne trade (widely cited; secondary).
primary_cargo: Crude oil & LNG (Gulf->Asia), containers, dry bulk (iron ore, coal, grain).
dominant_vessels: Container ships (25,127), bulk carriers (19,507), VLCCs (9,724), general cargo, LNG carriers (2024 counts).
top_users: China, Japan, South Korea (~80% of transiting crude), Indonesia.
local_economic_note: Singapore: world's largest bunkering hub (54.9M t marine fuel, 2024) and container transshipment port (41.1M TEU) (MPA).
reroute_note: Alternatives: Sunda (+1,086 nm / ~2 days) or Lombok (+2,488 nm / ~4 days) Straits (RSIS).

share_world_trade: ~20% of global petroleum liquids, ~25% of seaborne oil, and >20% of LNG trade (EIA; IEA).
primary_cargo: Crude oil & condensate, refined products, LNG.
dominant_vessels: Crude & product tankers (incl. VLCCs), LNG carriers.
top_users: Exporters: Saudi Arabia, Iraq, UAE, Iran, Kuwait, Qatar; destinations: China, India, Japan, South Korea (~74%).
local_economic_note: Vital to Gulf exporters; Qatar ~93% and UAE ~96% of LNG exports transit the strait (IEA).
reroute_note: Bypass pipelines (Saudi Petroline, UAE ADCOP) offer ~3.5-5 mb/d of spare capacity against ~21 mb/d of flow (IEA).

transit_basis: All vessels, 2023 baseline (~459 vessels/week, IMF PortWatch). Weekly transits fell ~48% in 2024 during the Red Sea crisis.
share_world_trade: ~10-12% of world trade via the Suez corridor; ~30% of global container traffic (UNCTAD).
primary_cargo: Containers, crude & products, dry bulk and grain (southern gateway to the Suez Canal).
dominant_vessels: Container ships, bulk carriers, oil tankers.
local_economic_note: Gateway feeding the Suez Canal; the 2024 crisis cut Suez revenue by ~US$7bn (SCA).
reroute_note: Alternative: Cape of Good Hope (+~4,000 nm / +10-14 days); the SUMED pipeline (~2.5 mb/d) bypasses only Suez-bound Gulf oil.

transit_basis: All vessels, 2024 (EIA, 'more than 45,000/yr' through the Bosphorus).
share_world_trade: ~5% of global maritime trade; the Black Sea region supplies ~30% of world wheat exports (EIA; FAO).
primary_cargo: Russian & Caspian crude and products, Black Sea grain, steel.
dominant_vessels: Oil & product tankers, dry bulk (grain) carriers, general cargo.
top_users: Kazakhstan, Russia, Azerbaijan (oil); Ukraine, Russia, Romania (grain).
local_economic_note: Only sea outlet for Black Sea states; passage governed by the 1936 Montreux Convention (Turkiye MFA).
reroute_note: No maritime bypass exists - the only sea route between the Black Sea and the world ocean.

transit_basis: Commercial vessels/day (UK Maritime & Coastguard Agency). Commonly cited as the world's busiest shipping lane.
share_world_trade: World's busiest shipping lane; the Port of Dover alone handles 33% of UK-EU goods trade (Port of Dover).
primary_cargo: Containers, RoRo freight & ferries, North Sea oil & LNG, grain, chemicals.
dominant_vessels: Cargo ships plus 100+ cross-Channel ferry/RoRo movements per day.
top_users: United Kingdom, France, Netherlands, Belgium, Germany.
local_economic_note: Gateway to the Rotterdam/Antwerp/Hamburg range; Port of Dover handled 8.9M passengers and 2.2M freight vehicles (2023).
reroute_note: No practical maritime bypass for Channel traffic; the Channel Tunnel carries some freight (2.6M vehicles, 2023).

transit_basis: All vessels/day (~148 merchant), attributed to the Gibraltar Port Authority via a secondary aggregator - treat as indicative (see confidence).
share_world_trade: Sole maritime gateway between the Mediterranean and the Atlantic; adjacent hubs handle ~15M TEU/yr (port authorities).
primary_cargo: Container transshipment (Algeciras, Tanger Med), crude & products, dry bulk, ferries.
dominant_vessels: Container ships, tankers, bulk carriers, ferries.
top_users: Spain, Morocco; EU-Asia and EU-Americas carriers.
local_economic_note: Serves the whole Mediterranean basin; Algeciras ~104M t and Tanger Med 10.2M TEU (2024).
reroute_note: No maritime bypass - the sole western sea entrance to the Mediterranean.
